results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the VFB database. VFB records show that the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, with different structures at different life stages. VFB holds various data related to the mushroom body, including images, neuron information, parts, and subclasses, which can be explored further. For example, VFB has annotated [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body and [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body.

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response:
To address the question about the main components of the Drosophila central complex and their associated functions, we must consider the available data and literature. However, given that the provided EVIDENCE and RESOLVED ENTITIES are empty, I must rely on general knowledge about Drosophila neuroscience.

The Drosophila central complex is a critical structure in the insect brain, known for its role in regulating various aspects of behavior and cognition, including locomotion, navigation, and spatial memory. It is composed of several distinct substructures, each with specific functions. These components typically include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the noduli, and the protocerebral bridge, among others.

The ellipsoid body is often associated with the integration of visual and motor information, playing a role in the control of locomotion and possibly in spatial orientation. The fan-shaped body is thought to be involved in the processing of spatial information and in the regulation of locomotor activities. The noduli and the protocerebral bridge are also implicated in spatial memory and navigation.

It's important to note that the specific functions and interactions of these components are subjects of ongoing research. For detailed and accurate information, consulting recent publications and databases such as FlyBase or specific neuroscience literature would be necessary.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as recorded in VFB. According to VFB, the giant fiber neuron has specific anatomy, including a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, and a large descending axon that enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. 

VFB records show that the giant fiber neuron has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The axon enters the ventral nerve cord near the dorsal midline and extends posteroventrally to the mesothoracic neuromere, where it turns ventrolaterally, and ends abruptly without branching.

The connectivity of the giant fiber neuron is further detailed in VFB, with downstream connectivity classes for DNp01 numbering [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01"), and upstream connectivity classes for DNp01 numbering [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01"). 

VFB holds [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of DNp01, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting DNp01, and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01, which may be useful for further study of the giant fiber neuron. 

Relevant publications, as cited in VFB, include Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), Power (1948), Ito et al. (2014), Kamikouchi et al. (2009), Matsuo et al. (2016), and Kim et al. (2020).

results.title: Concepts: NBLAST
results.question: What is NBLAST and what does an NBLAST similarity score mean?
results.response: NBLAST is a method to quantify morphological similarity. According to the documentation, its similarity score is calculated by finding the closest tangent vector in the target neuron for each tangent vector in the query neuron, and then summing over all query-target vector pairs, typically normalized to a self-self comparison with a perfect match being 1. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain documentation, which cites Costa et al., 2016. VFB does not currently hold additional data on the interpretation of NBLAST similarity scores beyond this documentation.
